'''Richard Dryden Field Jr.''' (born April 13, 1944) is an emeritus professor of [[physics]] at the [[University of Florida]] in [[Gainesville, Florida]].<ref name= "UFla">[https://www.phys.ufl.edu/wp/index.php/people/faculty/richard-field/ Rick Field profile], University of Florida website; accessed December 12, 2021.</ref> He is known particularly for his contributions to the phenomenology of particle production in high-energy particle accelerators.

==Education and personal life==
Field was born in [[Pasadena, California]], the son of actress [[Margaret Field]] and Richard Dryden Field, an Army officer. He was the stepson of actor/stuntman [[Jock Mahoney]]. His sister is Academy Award-winning actress [[Sally Field]]. Richard Field obtained his undergraduate education in [[physics]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] on a gymnastics scholarship,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/news/os-xpm-1986-12-14-0280130098-story.html|access-date=November 19, 2021|title = Rick Field|newspaper= [[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=14 December 1986 }} </ref> and continued with his PhD in 1971 under the supervision of [[John David Jackson (physicist)|John David Jackson]].

==Research==
Starting in 1971, he did post-doctoral work at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]. In 1973 he moved to [[California Institute of Technology]] to work with Nobel laureate [[Richard Feynman]].
It was there that he did his most-cited work, producing the "Field-Feynman" [[Monte Carlo method|Monte Carlo]] used to compare the production of observable particles arising from the fragmentation of [[quark]]s and [[gluon]]s in different particle accelerator environments. Two papers from this work,<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Field | first1 = R.D. | last2 = Feynman | first2 = R.P. | year = 1977 | title = Quark Elastic Scattering as a Source of High Transverse Momentum Mesons | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = D15 | issue = 9 | pages = 2590–2616 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2590| bibcode = 1977PhRvD..15.2590F | url = https://resolver.caltech.edu/CaltechAUTHORS:FIEprd77 | url-access = subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Field | first1 = R.D. | last2 = Feynman | first2 = R.P. | year = 1978 | title = A Parametrization of the Properties of Quark Jets | journal = Nuclear Physics | volume = B136 | issue = 1 | pages = 1–76 | doi=10.1016/0550-3213(78)90015-9| bibcode = 1978NuPhB.136....1F }}</ref> each with over 1000 citations, continue to be referenced {{asof|2021|lc=y}}.
<ref>{{cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/literature?sort=mostrecent&size=25&page=1&q=a%20r%20d%20field%20and%20ac%202%20and%20a%20feynman&ui-citation-summary=true|title = INSPIREHEP
|access-date=November 19, 2021}}</ref>

During this time he served as the PhD thesis advisor to computer-scientist/physicist [[Stephen Wolfram]], who is CEO of [[Wolfram Research]] and was considered a physics prodigy in his student years. In 1980, Field moved to the [[University of Florida]] as a professor and, later, emeritus professor.<ref name= "UFla"/>

==Honors==
He was elected a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 1987, "for contributions to the application of the Quantum Chromodynamic theory of quarks and gluons to hadron hadron collisions and the concept of parton fragmentation".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1987&unit_id=DPF&institution=University+of+Florida|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|access-date=November 19, 2021}}</ref>
